title: I cracked 8 dir walking animations but
author: Negative_Leave5161
selftext:
Which is hardest, it means other animations are solved. There are only few minor things I need to fix for self use. 

I want to know if there are enough interest for me to worth while commercialize it.

The product is NOT built yet so this isn’t a commercial post. I’m a SWE at its current state it is not friendly enough.

comments.author: PatagonianCowboy
comments.body: the pixel art doesn't look pixel perfect tho

comments.author: Economy_Drama_8757
comments.body: I'm actually very interested this. I've been playing around with creating a spritesheet for a game I'm developing and it's been annoying trying to get gpt-image-2.5 to recognize the left arm movement. It's the weirdest possible thing... I provide it a character, every other slice of the sheet is perfect. It's like it refuses to recognize the character has a left arm. lol

replies.author: Negative_Leave5161
replies.body: gpt-image-2.5 works for monsters with stubbed limbs, for something with proper legs nope. Seems the interest is low here though, I'll dm

replies.author: Savings_Cloud5486
replies.body: you should use video generation models for animations, not image ones

comments.author: yaxir
comments.body: can you also teach me please!!

comments.author: Capital-Divide
comments.body: Would love to know what you did

comments.author: TartNo3610
comments.body: Ive been wishing there was something like this. Would love to try this. Good work!

comments.author: PSloVR
comments.body: Other animations are solved?  How's that?

replies.author: Ruskarr
replies.body: I don't think it is either. The work of touching up "here and there" across 8 sprites and their frames quickly multiplies when you consider a general pack of what... Idle, death, melee attack, ranged cast, pick up loot, etc etc.

replies.author: PhilsburyDoboy
replies.body: Don’t forget changing equipment - even just coloring the clothes or weapon differently.

replies.author: wardrol_
replies.body: I would belive he is referring to other animations of his project.

comments.author: MrShamus
comments.body: Very cool, have had issues and would def be interested

replies.author: Professor_Snipe
replies.body: You can generate a lower quality video from your concept art on green background for almost free, with a strict prompt you can get really crazy, crisp consistent animations that you then turn into sprites.

replies.author: Aznshorty13
replies.body: What do you use for video gen to get almost free?

comments.author: KeenAsGreen
comments.body:
Some of these look really rough. Especially walking east. 

You won't be able to commercialise this. Pixel lab only charge like $10 a month for 2000 sprite sheet generations

replies.author: FazedEclipse2
replies.body:
Commercialise...or sell for a pretty penny...

Cause theres a difference, and plenty of games less than a fiver with worse animations that people buy

comments.author: moonblade89
comments.body: The true test is asymmetry. Put a weapon in one hand and see if its consistently in the correct hand from all angles. Thats where previous tools have fallen apart

comments.author: RafaSC00
comments.body: wooow i like it, really nice job

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: The final test is achieving a target visual that couldn't be achieved by the approach of making 3D model that are then post-processed into pixel art from various camera angles. That one specific example you have here could be done like this.

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body: Personally I'm sick of everyone trying to monetise on top of the backs of open source. Stop being greedy, GIVE BACK. Advance the community on solving these problems and make everyone's lives better. If you try to monetise you will just be lost in the depths of the 1000 other people claiming the same

comments.author: _Diocletian_
comments.body: Give me 8 dirs walking animations butt

comments.author: wirthmore
comments.body: The timing of poses should be aligned. For example if you pause the video, the character should have the right foot in the same position across all views.

comments.author: chiezyy
comments.body: Isn't that exactly what pixellab does?

comments.author: Bluetails_Buizel
comments.body: The next part is to figure out how to make the art style less like ai
